classification.classification_note: The saved ASan report is a bad-free in `xmlFreeNodeList` reached from `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` while schema parsing expands an internal entity through `xmlParseReference`. The freed address lies inside a dictionary allocation created through `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`, but the staged source here does not prove the exact source-level assignment that copied that dictionary-backed pointer into the later-freed node field. This GT therefore anchors the causal bug on the missing well-formedness guard and keeps the allocation context as runtime evidence rather than asserting an unproven aliasing statement.

bug_description.original: An invalid-free in libxml2's parser (parser.c) causes xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeNode to attempt to free an address that was not obtained from malloc. The error occurs during reference/balanced-chunk parsing (xmlParseReference / xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal), leading to crashes and potential heap corruption when processing crafted XML (e.g., schema) inputs.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The witnessed schema input is parsed with `SCHEMAS_PARSE_OPTIONS`, so document content expansion reaches `xmlParseReference`. When the crafted entity reference is encountered, `xmlParseEntityRef` returns an internal general entity but also leaves `ctxt->wellFormed == 0`. In the vulnerable commit, `xmlParseReference` does not stop on that failed parser state and still calls `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` on `ent->content`. The balanced-chunk parser reports failure and then unconditionally frees its temporary pseudoroot with `xmlFreeNode(ctxt->myDoc->children)`, which recurses into `xmlFreeNodeList` and reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`. ASan proves that the freed pointer is an interior address inside a dictionary allocation created from `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`, so the malformed entity drives generic node cleanup over storage that was not malloc-owned for direct `free()`.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed crashing path that consumes the crafted entity reference and materializes the entity object plus the failed well-formedness state later ignored by the vulnerable continuation.
source.value_from: After schema parsing is admitted with `XML_PARSE_NOENT`, document content reaches `xmlParseReference`. The saved witness drives `xmlParseEntityRef(ctxt)` to return an internal general entity and the subsequent patch shows that the missing guard is the immediately following `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;`.

sink.description: ASan sink. Recursive cleanup of the temporary balanced-chunk tree frees a node-name pointer with `DICT_FREE`, and ASan reports that pointer as not malloc-owned.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at `tree.c:3750`, and the staged vulnerable source shows line 3750 is the `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` branch inside `xmlFreeNodeList`. ASan also reports that freed address as an interior pointer inside a region allocated by `xmlDictAddString` from `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`.

root_cause.description: After `xmlParseEntityRef` has already left the parser not well formed, the vulnerable code continues into entity expansion instead of aborting that path.
root_cause.note: The fix inserts `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` immediately before this line, so the missing guard is the direct source-level obligation that allows the later bad-free path to execute.

tainted_value_origin.note: Harness context only. The schema fuzz target constructs a schema parser context and invokes `xmlSchemaParse`, but the scored source is the project-side entity-reference consumption inside `xmlParseReference`, not the libFuzzer entry boundary.

parser_admitted.description: The testcase is admitted as a schema document and parsed with `SCHEMAS_PARSE_OPTIONS`, which enables entity expansion and reaches normal XML content parsing rather than rejecting the file before the vulnerable reference path.

coarse_trace.summary: Schema loading admits the testcase and parses it with entity expansion enabled.
An entity reference is resolved, and the parser is already left not well formed on the witnessed path.
The vulnerable code ignores that failed state and still parses the entity replacement text as a balanced chunk.
The balanced-chunk parser reports failure but still tears down its temporary tree with generic node cleanup.
Recursive node destruction reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` and triggers the bad-free ASan reports.

fine_trace.note: Source. While parsing admitted schema content with entity expansion enabled, the crafted reference is resolved into `ent`; on the witnessed path this call also leaves `ctxt->wellFormed == 0` before control returns to `xmlParseReference`.

Root cause. The vulnerable code continues past the failed well-formedness state from step 1 instead of returning immediately. The patch adds `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` directly before this line.

Because step 2 did not stop the path, libxml2 parses the malformed internal entity replacement text as a balanced chunk and produces temporary parser state that will later be torn down through `list` and the pseudoroot tree.
Inside the balanced-chunk subparser, the malformed entity content is recognized as a parse failure, so `ret` is set to an error rather than `XML_ERR_OK`.

Even on the failed parse path from step 4, the subparser unconditionally frees its temporary pseudoroot subtree. The ASan crash stack shows this exact cleanup site immediately above `xmlFreeNodeList` on the witness path.

depends_on.via: temporary pseudoroot tree built from ent->content

fine_trace.note: Sink. Recursive destruction of that temporary subtree reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`, and ASan reports the target address as an interior pointer inside a dictionary allocation from `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`, making this a bad free of non-malloc-owned storage.

depends_on.via: xmlFreeNode recurses into xmlFreeNodeList on children

poc.trigger: The saved testcase is the exact schema input reproduced by `./fuzz/schema /gt/poc`. Grounded by the staged source and saved ASan traces, this witness admits schema parsing, expands an internal general entity, leaves `ctxt->wellFormed == 0` after `xmlParseEntityRef`, still enters `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal(ent->content, ..., &list)`, and then crashes during temporary-tree cleanup at `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`.

format.name: libxml2-schema-fuzzer
format.contract: The validated trigger is the saved witness that causes `xmlParseEntityRef(ctxt)` to return an internal general entity while also leaving `ctxt->wellFormed == 0`, so vulnerable `xmlParseReference` still calls `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal(ent->content, ..., &list)` and the balanced-chunk cleanup later reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`. This GT stays at that witnessed contract and does not generalize beyond the saved input or claim an unobserved source-level alias assignment into `cur->name`.
